_about.why: set4 was curated over the nostoc community graphs. Eleven of its axis endpoints are not nodes in the EPI300 host graph at all, so those axes measure a structural zero on every construction -- which in a scored table is indistinguishable from a real null. Each entry here names the members this host DOES carry. A substitution is a fact about a HOST, not about set4, which is why this file is named for one and set4 is untouched.
_about.rule: Among members of the declared family that the host graph carries, rank by the number of host-nominated reactions incident on the metabolite. For the phospholipids, restrict first to genuine DIACYL species -- a concrete formula with no `*` residue and at least 30 carbons, which is two acyl chains plus the glycerophospho backbone. That restriction is load-bearing: the highest-degree PE-named member the host carries is MNXM1364224 at 22 reactions, and its formula is C5H14NO6P, the deacylated headgroup rather than a phospholipid at all.
_about.two_members_not_one: Where the top of a family is not a clear winner, both are carried and the axis is measured twice. That is this arm's own rule for an unmakeable choice -- the same reason it draws two null sampler styles mismatched in opposite directions -- and it turns the choice into a measured spread instead of an argument. C18:1 and C16:0 rank first and second in BOTH phospholipid families here, and they are E. coli's two dominant membrane acyl chains.
_about.the_generic_stays: The declared id is never removed. It rides along as a control row, so a later bake that brings it into the host graph shows up as the control coming alive rather than as a silent change of meaning.
